bindings.confirmation: The record is now on screen for the person.
bindings.description: Show a structured record on screen: a person, an order, a file, anything with labeled fields. Use instead of a markdown table when the person should read one thing at a glance.

fields.description: The fields, in the order they should be read

value.description: Already formatted for a person to read

status.description: A short status word, e.g. Approved

statusTone.description: How this reads at a glance. Use negative and caution sparingly, for a refusal, a breach or a failure, not for anything merely notable.

subtitle.description: One line of context under the title

title.description: What this record is, e.g. a person or an order

bindings.title: Record

bindings.confirmation: The figures are now on screen for the person.
bindings.description: Show up to six figures with labels. Use when the person should compare numbers, not when a table or a full report is needed.

metrics.description: Up to six figures. More than that wanted a table.

change.description: The movement, e.g. '+12% on last month'

changeTone.description: How this reads at a glance. Use negative and caution sparingly, for a refusal, a breach or a failure, not for anything merely notable.

value.description: Already formatted, including any unit or currency

bindings.title: Figures

bindings.confirmation: The checklist is now on screen for the person.
bindings.description: Show a read-only checklist. Use for a set of items and whether each is already done. Do not use this for Todoist tasks the person should complete — use show_todoist_tasks for those.

items.description: The items, in the order they should be done

done.description: Whether this one is already finished

note.description: A short aside, e.g. who it is waiting on

bindings.title: Checklist

bindings.confirmation: The quotation is now on screen for the person.
bindings.description: Show a quotation with its attribution. Use when the exact words matter, something a person said, or a line from a document you were given.

attribution.description: Who said or wrote it, e.g. 'Grace Hopper' or 'the 2026 annual report'

context.description: One short line of context: where it is from, or why it matters here

quote.description: The quotation itself, without surrounding quote marks

bindings.title: Quotation
